sentences.text: Saurichthys is an extinct genus of prehistoric ray-finned fish belonging to the order Saurichthyiformes.
This elongate, streamlined fish typically measured between 0.6 and 1 meter in length.
While some species were only a few decimeters long, others could reach approximately 1.5 meters in length, such as a specimen from the Middle Triassic of Turkey.
The animal possessed extremely long jaws that constituted one-third of its total body length and terminated in a sharp, beak-like tip.
Its dorsal and anal fins were positioned opposite each other near the rear of the body, and it had a symmetrical, abbreviated diphycercal tail.
Fossils of pregnant females provide evidence that Saurichthys was viviparous, representing the oldest known example of this trait in ray-finned fishes.
Specialized pelvic fin rays or ventral scales in certain species are interpreted as male copulatory organs, providing evidence for internal fertilization.
The genus Saurichthys was first described by Louis Agassiz in 1834.
The oldest known fossils of Saurichthys come from the Wordie Creek Formation in East Greenland and date to the Early Triassic (Griesbachian/Induan stage).
Zhang et al. (2026) reported the first fossil evidence of Saurichthys in the Early Triassic Nanzhang-Yuan'an fauna in China.
Saurichthys is interpreted as an ambush predator, exhibiting behavior similar to modern gars and needlefish.
Fossil evidence of bone boluses suggests that Saurichthys either attacked marine reptiles like Langobardisaurus or scavenged their remains.
Studies of the gastrointestinal tract reveal that Saurichthys had a spiral valve with many windings, similar to present-day sharks and rays.
Saurichthys is classified in the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Actinopterygii, order Saurichthyiformes, and family Saurichthyidae.
Saurichthys was an extinct predatory ray-finned fish that lived during the Triassic Period.
Saurichthys lived in both marine and freshwater environments.
Saurichthys fossils date from the Capitanian to the Bathonian, spanning 264.28 to 165.3 million years ago.
While historically classified as close relatives of sturgeons and paddlefish within Chondrostei, modern studies suggest Saurichthys may lie outside the Actinopterygii crown group.
